findings.summary: A source-only excuse turns off the content check for a whole file, and 6 of the 7 terms use one on every file that gets scanned. In practice only Hermes, the case already fixed, is checked against its sources.
findings.evidence: In sense_problems, an excuse with `source` set and no `marker` matches every line of that file (`e.marker.as_deref().is_none_or(..)`). Decision-id sources are skipped, so these terms have every scanned file excused: planning (BRIEF.md, job-planning.md), job (BRIEF.md, records.md), Athena (BRIEF.md; D01 is skipped, so its `senses` list is never consulted), product versus system (both of its files), landed (BRIEF.md and native-pr-landing.md; its other source, D10, is skipped) and Sri (BRIEF.md). The excuse hides real candidate senses. BRIEF.md:11 says 'Athena: the orchestration system you build', which the definition contradicts ('Athena is not the whole system'). BRIEF.md:22 uses `athena` as the repo name. The Athena excuse itself mentions a third use ('the studied instance in Part 2') and waves it through instead of listing it. BRIEF.md is append-only and is where new senses arrive, and for every term except Hermes it is fully excused, so a new second sense there passes silently. That is the same failure class the request says to prevent. Any new term can pass the same way by adding one blanket excuse, which brings back the prose-only guard that D152 rejects. Simpler, more correct alternative: excuses must name a marker (per hit or phrase, as the introspection proposed, 'records why a hit is not one'), and source-wide excuses are refused for BRIEF.md or dropped altogether. The real terms then get the senses and markers they need (Athena already has senses that would do most of the work).
findings.location: docs/ontology.toml (excused entries on planning, job, Athena, product versus system, landed, Sri); crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs sense_problems excused predicate

findings.summary: Sense markers are plain substring matches tuned to the current lines, so lines get attributed to a sense because of an unrelated word.
findings.evidence: Hermes markers include 'stud' (matches any 'study'/'studied'), 'firstmate' (any line that also mentions firstmate counts as the Hermes Agent sense), and 'Hermes is mostly' (copied from one line, BRIEF.md:136). Athena markers include 'role' (matches 'control'), 'code' and 'build': BRIEF.md:11 would count as the program sense only because it contains 'build'. D152 notes the substring weakness as a tradeoff. Alternative: match markers as whole words, using names_term, and prefer markers that describe the sense over phrases copied from single lines.
findings.location: docs/ontology.toml Hermes and Athena senses; crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs sense_problems

findings.summary: Excuses that match nothing are not flagged, so stale excuses pile up unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Nothing checks that an excused entry matched at least one line. For example, landed's BRIEF.md excuse is kept even though BRIEF.md is not one of landed's sources. Flagging unused excuses would keep the record honest.

summary: The candidate fails. The new check itself works: the ontology test now reads BRIEF.md and each term's source files and flags any line naming a term that matches no listed sense and no excuse with a reason. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology` and all 14 tests passed, including scratch-file tests of the Hermes case (only the tool listed: flagged; both senses listed: passes). The decision D152 and the CHANGELOG entry name the cause and cite both jobs. Only the four expected files changed, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed, so all seven criteria are met. The verdict fails on one major soundness finding. An excuse can name a whole file with no marker, which silences every line in it, and 6 of the 7 terms have every scanned file excused that way. In practice only Hermes, the case that was already fixed, is checked. The excuses hide real candidate senses: BRIEF.md:11 calls Athena 'the orchestration system', which the definition contradicts, and BRIEF.md:22 uses `athena` as the repo name. BRIEF.md is append-only and is where new senses arrive, and for every term except Hermes it is never checked, so the failure class can recur. The fix is to require a marker on every excuse, or at least refuse whole-file excuses for BRIEF.md, and give the real terms proper senses. A minor issue: markers match as plain substrings, so 'stud', 'firstmate' and 'role' attribute lines to a sense because of unrelated words.
